title: Dataset loaders, fixtures, and fastpaths for eval harness
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note collects pragmatic patterns for lightweight dataset loaders, small deterministic fixtures (fastpaths) for onboarding new models, scoring shim implementations, and CI wiring for early regressions. The goal is to have a tiny, repeatable smoke surface that engineers can use locally and that CI will run quickly, while keeping the full eval harness available for nightly runs.

Why this differs from current docs:
- Prior docs focus on full eval runner and loader ecosystems. This is intentionally small: minimal deps, emphasis on deterministic seeds, tokenization parity checks, and fail-fast CI checks.
- Covers practical issues we repeatedly hit: tokenization drift between tokenizers, stochastic outputs, cache poisoning when using golden prompts, and how to surface flaky tests.

Key concepts / definitions:
- fastpath: a 5-30 example fixture (input/output pairs) per capability used for quick onboarding and PR-level smoke tests.
- loader shim: ~1-file adapter per dataset format that converts into the harness standard: {"id": str, "inputs": [str], "annotations": [str or dict], "meta": {}}
- scorer shim: a small callable that accepts (preds, golds, meta) and returns a dict of scalar metrics (strings->floats). Keep scoring deterministic and tiny for CI.
- token parity check: a pre-check that ensures the model/tokenizer combination yields expected token counts for golden prompts to catch tokenizer mismatch early.

Filesystem patterns (recommended layout inside evals repo):
- scripts/fastpaths/
  - create_fixture.py  # helper to build small JSONL fixtures from a dataset or manual inputs
- evals/loaders/
  - shim_<dataset>.py  # one-file loader shim, importable by eval runner
- evals/scorers/
  - basic_exact.py
  - f1_span.py (minimal dependency)
- ci/
  - smoke-eval.yaml  # small pipeline that runs fastpath fixtures against the deployed model

Loader shim template (pseudo):
def load(path_or_id):
    """Return list of records where each record is a flat dict with string fields."""
    out = []
    for line in open(path_or_id):
        raw = json.loads(line)
        out.append({"id": raw.get('uid') or str(uuid4()),
                    "inputs": [raw['text']],
                    "annotations": raw.get('gold') or [],
                    "meta": {"source": 'shim-xyz'} })
    return out

Notes on loader robustness:
- Avoid loading entire datasets into memory in CI; yield generators or stream and provide a --limit flag.
- Normalization: ensure homogenzied whitespace, unicode NFC, and ASCII punctuation normalization as a pre-step. We had multiple regressions caused by different apostrophe chars between golds and predictions.
- Tokenizer mismatch: include a small test that compares len(tokenizer.encode(golden_prompt)) against an expected count stored in the fixture (token_parity). Failing the test should open a ticket for tokenizer binding.

Fastpath fixture guidelines:
- Keep to at most 30 records per capability; prefer 10-15 for CI.
- Mix of positive/negative, boundary cases, and obvious errors the model should not make.
- For generative outputs, include multiple acceptable golds when possible or use normalized matching (strip punctuation, lower, simple paraphrase list).
- Each fixture should carry metadata: "seed" (random seed used if sampling), "token_parity" (list of token counts), "creation_commit".

Scoring functions and hooks:
- Scorers must be pure (no randomness) and fast. Keep complexity to O(n) per record.
- Return a map: {"score_name": float, ...} so CI can fail on named thresholds.
- Implement a tiny comparator utility: passes = comparator(pred, golds, strategy="norm") where strategy in [exact, token_overlap, normalized_f1].
- Expose a "explain" mode to return why a record failed (diff-ish) to show in CI artifacts.

CI wiring (smoke-eval.yaml) sketch:
- triggered: on PR to main (targeted at model-serving changes or eval runner changes)
- job: run-fastpath-evals
  - checkout repo
  - setup pyenv/venv, install minimal deps (requests, tokenizers, numpy)
  - run: python -m scripts.fastpaths.run --fixtures=ci/fastpaths/* --target=${DEPLOYED_MODEL_ENDPOINT} --timeout=60 --max-records=15 --report=ci/artifacts/fastpath-report.json
  - upload artifacts on failure: report json, per-record failure traces, token parity diffs
- time budget: <10 minutes, prefer <3 minutes.

Determinism and flaky tests:
- For generative models, pin temperature=0 when possible for CI. If CI must test stochastic behavior, do N=5 runs and require median metric >= threshold and stdev < small_eps.
- Watch for non-determinism from external calls (e.g., remote tokenizer libraries with multi-threaded randomness). Use single-thread env var if needed.

Regression reporting and triage:
- Report schema (fastpath-report.json):
  - overall: {"scores": {name: val}, "status": pass|warn|fail }
  - per_record: list of {id, inputs, golds, pred, score_map, explain}
  - meta: fixture, commit, job_id, model_hash, tokenizer_hash
- Triage workflow: auto-open regression draft in Slack channel #eval-regressions with minimal info and link to artifact. If metric drop >5% absolute, create JIRA AI-REG-xxx with failure archetype and assign to model onboarding owner.

Common pitfalls we've seen:
1) Tokenization drift: model uses SentencePiece vs. fixture uses HuggingFace tokenizer; parity test would have caught this.
2) Golden sample leakage: caching layer returns training-set exact outputs; add cache-buster meta or blind test queries.
3) Locale/Unicode differences: normalize to NFC and fix quotes.
4) Overfitting fastpath: if fastpath too small and specifically tuned, we end up with brittle gating; rotate fixtures monthly and keep a separate small holdout.

Mini-checklist for onboarding a new model (fast path):
- [ ] build 10-20 record fastpath fixtures for core capabilities
- [ ] add loader shim if dataset format is new; include --limit and --seed flags
- [ ] implement token_parity and add expected counts to fixture
- [ ] add scorer shim (one metric per capability for CI) and thresholds
- [ ] add entry to ci/smoke-eval.yaml to run the new fixture
- [ ] run locally with --report and inspect artifacts; iterate until stable
- [ ] push PR with fixture + loader + scorer + CI change, request review from applied-ml and platform-eng

Open questions / TODOs:
- How granular should per-route timeouts be? (model vs single-record timeout)
- Do we allow nonzero temp in PR CI for semantic fuzz checks? (proposal: no, but nightly stochastic runs allowed)
- Should we canonicalize on a single tokenizer package for all fixtures to avoid mismatch? (tradeoff: ease vs fidelity to model runtime)

Notes to self / small cheatsheet commands:
- Build fixture from existing dataset (one-liner): python scripts/fastpaths/create_fixture.py --dataset path/to/data.jsonl --out ci/fastpaths/newcap.jsonl --limit 15 --seed 42
- Run local fastpath: python -m scripts.fastpaths.run --fixtures ci/fastpaths/newcap.jsonl --target http://localhost:8080/generate --max-records 15 --report /tmp/report.json
- Quick token parity: python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('hf-tokenizer.json'); print([len(t.encode(x).ids) for x in open('ci/fastpaths/newcap.jsonl')])"

Slack / PR references:
- see thread: slack://team/applied-ml/C02ABC123/thread-evallocs (use this when filing regressions)
- related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/412 - implements the smoke runner and base scorers

If you pick this up: start by creating one tiny fastpath fixture for the most-used hosted-api capability (completion) and wire it through the smoke CI. Keep it tiny; iterate.

End.
